title: The Sum of Our Technology
summary: What if AI acceleration fails outside a code generator? Two shifts in software engineering demand evidence, sustainable delivery and viable socio-technical control.

rights.notice: Article by Vitalii Oborskyi; author-selected AI-generated Cover 02 and seven original full-page PMDay v35 slide screenshots. Original source-deck and third-party credits remain applicable. Per-item publication clearance remains pending.

assets.caption: We can delegate more work. We still have to own the consequences.

assets.alt: Synthetic capacities: generation rises from eight to one hundred changes per week while review and integration remain at eight; the queue grows by ninety-two if every change is admitted.
assets.caption: Synthetic fixed-capacity illustration. Uncontrolled intake accumulates work; controlled intake bounds the queue without proportionally increasing delivery. Both regimes are explained in the text. PMDay 2026 · slide 3 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 3 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Illustrative generation and comprehension curves diverge, showing a possible overload scenario rather than a measured human limit.
assets.caption: An illustrative overload hypothesis, not a measured limit on cognition. Tools and learning can change the team’s comprehension capacity. PMDay 2026 · slide 5 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 5 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Measurement and candidate countermeasures for finding a sustainable AI-assisted SDLC equilibrium.
assets.caption: Measures and candidate responses, not universally validated remedies. Faster generation alone does not establish a sustainable new equilibrium. PMDay 2026 · slide 7 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 7 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Acceptable answers, clarification and escalation occupy a bounded response space; unauthorised disclosure is outside it.
assets.caption: The drawing is schematic, not a probability map. Answering, clarifying or escalating can all be correct; unauthorised disclosure remains outside the boundary. PMDay 2026 · slide 9 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 9 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Synthetic evaluation: 196 acceptable responses, three incorrect recovery instructions and one unauthorised disclosure.
assets.caption: Synthetic 196 / 3 / 1 outcomes. The slide’s four-failure interval concerns all failures; the article separately calculates uncertainty for the one critical disclosure. PMDay 2026 · slide 10 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 10 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Model proposals pass fallible semantic checks and enforced permissions; denials, fallback, observation and authorised intervention form a control loop.
assets.caption: Permissions, evidence, fallible semantic checks and verified intervention form one operating path. Real human capacity and response time must be supplied and tested. PMDay 2026 · slide 12 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 12 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.

assets.alt: Delivery commitments continue alongside an experiment-and-reassessment loop informed by production outcomes and incidents.
assets.caption: Production observations and incidents update assumptions and controls. Learning does not suspend delivery or service obligations.  PMDay 2026 · slide 14 · Vitalii Oborskyi. [1]
assets.credit: Full-page screenshot of PMDay 2026 v35 review slide 14 by Vitalii Oborskyi. Source-deck and third-party credits preserved; publication rights pending.
